evals.prompt: We are building a recipe-sharing app and have a pile of ideas: meal planning, grocery lists, a social feed, importing recipes from other websites, and nutrition tracking. Some of them clearly depend on each other and I cannot decide what to build next. Help me break this down and pick something. The product is for home cooks who often cook with poor signal, and I do not want to touch payments or delivery at all.
evals.expected_output: A grouped set of outcomes with dependencies, a lightweight backlog, and exactly one recommended focus awaiting approval, with no tasks, estimates, or code.
expectations: The prioritize skill is invoked without the user naming it
Existing instructions and project documents (backlog, work-in-progress, changelog) are checked before the user is asked to repeat facts
The refine skill is called with its design tree rooted in choosing the next focus
Ideas are grouped into vertical user outcomes (for example 'cooks can build a shopping list') instead of layers such as 'all database work'
Each dependency is marked as confirmed or suspected, and cycles or unresolved shared prerequisites are stated
documentation/backlog.md has Direction, Outcomes, and Out of scope sections, with payments and delivery under Out of scope with the user's reason
Every outcome carries one of candidate, approved now, approved for later, or deferred
Exactly one focus is recommended, with its value, prerequisites, what is deferred, and what would change the recommendation
No tasks, estimates, requirements, or application code are produced
The run ends by telling the user they can run /iterate to build the focus

evals.prompt: Use the prioritize skill on the attached project (treat recipe-app as the repository root). Offline support feels more urgent than the shared-list work that is in progress. What do you think we should do?
evals.expected_output: The agent recommends, then waits for explicit confirmation before replacing the active work, and keeps the replaced work's resumption information.
expectations: documentation/backlog.md, work-in-progress.md, and CHANGELOG.md are read before any recommendation
The recommendation weighs the offline outcome against the in-progress shared-list work, naming prerequisites and what would change the recommendation
work-in-progress.md is not modified until the user explicitly confirms replacing the active work
After confirmation, the replaced work's progress and open question (the household member who leaves) are kept as resumption information rather than deleted
The selected backlog heading, the approval, constraints, and remaining prerequisites are recorded in work-in-progress.md
The approval is recorded as an Agreement in CHANGELOG.md because it changes priorities
The other candidate outcomes remain unapproved: approving offline does not approve the next outcome
No application code, dependency, or external tracker is touched

evals.prompt: Use the prioritize skill. Candidate outcomes for our recipe app: (a) push notifications that remind cooks when to start a recipe, (b) offline saved recipes, (c) a weekly planner. Whether (a) is even possible depends on what installed web apps are allowed to do on iPhones, and I do not know the current rules.
evals.expected_output: The external unknown goes to research with a bounded question while shaping continues, and the dependent outcome stays a named blocker until evidence arrives.
expectations: The agent calls the research skill with a bounded question about push notification support for installed web apps on iPhones
Independent shaping of outcomes (b) and (c) continues while the research runs
Outcome (a) is marked with its dependency as suspected and is not ranked until the evidence arrives
If the evidence has not arrived, the unknown stays a named blocker with its pending question in the backlog
The recommended focus is either an independent outcome or resolving the bounded question first, and the agent states which

evals.prompt: Use the prioritize skill on the attached project (treat recipe-app as the repository root). We dropped the social feed idea for good because moderation is too expensive. The weekly meal planner already shipped, as the changelog shows. Revisit the backlog and tell me what is next, but I will not decide until tomorrow.
evals.expected_output: The backlog is reconciled with actual progress, only affected entries change, and the focus remains an explicitly pending proposal.
expectations: Actual progress is reconciled from CHANGELOG.md and work-in-progress.md before reprioritizing
The completed meal planner outcome keeps a pointer to its result (CHG-0002) instead of being deleted
The social feed moves to Out of scope with the user's reason (moderation cost)
Only the affected backlog entries change; unrelated outcomes are left as they were
A single focus is proposed, and the proposal and its open decision are stated as pending approval
work-in-progress.md is not rewritten to a new active focus, because the user has not approved one

evals.prompt: We are moving our billing from a legacy payment provider to a new one. We do not yet know the migration approach, which compliance rules apply, or what shape our stored customer data is in. This will take several sessions of research, prototypes, and interviews. Chart out the questions we need to settle.
evals.expected_output: The open question is design and feasibility over several sessions, not which outcome comes first, so the request belongs to graphify.
expectations: The prioritize skill is not invoked and no outcome backlog is written
The agent tells the user /graphify fits better, or uses it, to chart a decision map toward a named destination

evals.prompt: The household sharing feature is specified and approved. Split it into implementation tasks with acceptance criteria and blockers so the team can pick them up.
evals.expected_output: Agreed behavior needing delivery tasks belongs to taskify.
expectations: The prioritize skill is not invoked and no backlog or focus is rewritten
The agent uses the taskify skill, or names it as the right tool, to produce tasks with acceptance criteria and explicit blocking dependencies
